title: Ordinary etale projective-line adjunction with arbitrary finite invertible-exponent coefficients
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of rings whose ascending chains of ideals stabilize) on which $N$ is invertible. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ with projection $q:P\to S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Work on small ordinary etale sites and their entire derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For each scheme $T$ over $S$ define the ordinary etale sheaf $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$, with $\mu_N$ and its action as in [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Write $\mathbf G_{m,P}$ for the sheaf $U\mapsto\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$ and $\mathcal O_P(1)$ for the line bundle whose local generators $g_0,g_1$ on $D(x_0),D(x_1)$ satisfy $g_0=(x_1/x_0)^{-1}g_1$. Let $h:A_S\to Rq_*A_P(1)[2]$ be the scalar-extended Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ (apply the connecting homomorphism of the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] to the line-bundle class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$, then extend scalars from $\mathbf Z/N$ to $A$ and use inverse-image/direct-image adjunction). The map whose components are the shifted, twisted unit and $h$ is an isomorphism
$$b_q:A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*A_P(1)[2].$$
Define $t_q=\operatorname{pr}_2 b_q^{-1}$, so $t_qh=1$. There is an adjunction on the entire ordinary etale derived categories
$$Rq_*\dashv G_q,\qquad G_qK=q^{-1}K\otimes_A^L A_P(1)[2],$$
whose actual counit is
$$\epsilon_{q,K}:Rq_*G_qK\xrightarrow{\pi^{-1}_{q,K,A_P(1)[2]}}K\otimes_A^LRq_*A_P(1)[2]\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_q}K,$$
where $\pi$ is the canonical proper tensor projection map of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and the last target uses the tensor unit constraint. The decomposition, trace and this adjunction normalization commute with base change between Noetherian $S$-schemes under the canonical ordinary-etale proper exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. No pro-etale or inverse-limit twist occurs in this assertion.

source.place: Agent-written ordinary-etale coefficient interface for the diagonal-kernel proof; decomposition and trace in thm-amb-p1-decomposition.md and def-amb-p1-trace.md; Kummer sequence: Stacks Tag 03PL, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-kummer-sequence; unbounded proper exchange: Tag 0F0C, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n, extended to torsion rings

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z/N$. Work throughout on ordinary small etale sites. Both coefficient rings to which the projection theorem is applied are finite commutative rings: $R=\mathbf Z/N$ is finite and $A$ is finite by hypothesis. Its $r^*$ is exactly the termwise inverse image $r^{-1}$ used here. In all steps below, the ordered projection map is the symmetry-conjugate of the adjoint-of-counit map, exactly as specified in [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]; thus the inverse in the stated counit uses this specified map. The projections $q:P\to S$ and $p_a:P\times_SP\to P$ are projective-line projections, hence proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. They have finite type and Noetherian sources, so the arbitrary-complex projection formula of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] applies. The standard opens of $\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[x_0,x_1]$ are supplied by [def-nagata-affine-proj]. Their degree-zero rings are $\mathbf Z[x_1/x_0]$ and $\mathbf Z[x_0/x_1]$: every degree-zero monomial fraction is a power of the indicated ratio, and those powers are independent. Pull back this cover through the base-change definition of $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], tensoring these rings with $B$ gives $B[t]$ and $B[s]$. Explicitly over each affine Noetherian open of $S$, the two charts are $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B[s]$; their product charts are $\operatorname{Spec}B[t,u]$. [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes these finite-type sources locally Noetherian; the finite charts over the finite affine cover of the Noetherian base make them quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. The diagonal is closed because $q$ is separated (part of properness); [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a) makes it proper and of finite type. Every exchange needed below is invertible on the entire derived category by [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring], with $R$ or $A$: both are killed by $N$. The twist-line lemma [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] makes $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}$ locally free of rank one over $R_T$, and makes $A_T(1)$ locally free of rank one over $A_T$. In particular the twists are flat. Pullback preserves their equations and their scalar-extension description. None of this uses an adic twist.

source.place: Hypotheses for the diagonal construction and proper exchange

proof.text: First prove the decomposition over $R$. At a geometric point $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$, with $k$ algebraically closed, the fibre is $\mathbf P^1_k$. By [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero] it is a smooth proper connected curve of genus zero. Choose a primitive $N$th root using [lem-sc-primitive-root]. Apply [thm-sc-proper-cohomology] with $g=0$: the constant $R$-cohomology is $R$ in degrees $0,2$ and zero otherwise. The primitive root identifies $\mu_N$ with that constant sheaf, so the same vanishing holds for $\mu_N$, with $H^0=\mu_N(k)$. To check the degree-two component rather than just its rank, [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors] identifies $H^2(P_k,\mu_N)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(P_k)/N$ by the actual Kummer boundary. The split degree sequence [lem-sc-pic-proper-decomposition] and $N$-divisibility of $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ from [lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion] identify this quotient with $\mathbf Z/N$ by degree. The divisor $x_1=0$ is one $k$-rational point. Its ideal generators on $D(x_0)$ and $D(x_1)$ are $t=x_1/x_0$ and $1$; their dual generators satisfy $g_0=t^{-1}g_1$, so its line bundle is the specified $\mathcal O(1)$. Its degree is one by [def-sc-pic0]. Thus $h_R$ induces the isomorphism $R\to H^2(P_k,\mu_N)$ taking $1$ to degree one. The twisted shifted unit induces the identity on $H^0(P_k,\mu_N)$. Proper exchange [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] gives these computations on the geometric stalks of the cohomology of $b_{q,R}$. Exactness of stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] make every cohomology map invertible. The unbounded cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves $b_{q,R}$ invertible.

Apply derived scalar extension $A\otimes_R^L-$ to $b_{q,R}$. To identify its target use the projection formula of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] with its finite coefficient ring specialized to $R=\mathbf Z/N$, with $K=A_S$ regarded as an $R$-module complex and $L=\mu_{N,P}[2]$. It gives $A_S\otimes_R^LRq_*\mu_{N,P}[2]\cong Rq_*(A_P\otimes_R^L\mu_{N,P})[2]$. The twist-line lemma makes $\mu_N$ flat, so $A_P\otimes_R^L\mu_{N,P}=A_P(1)$, even if $A$ is not $R$-flat. For precision construct the comparison inside $D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ as follows, rather than trying to lift a morphism of $R$-complexes. Write $e_T^* = A_T\otimes_{R_T}^L-$ for the derived module pullback of the identity topos with ring map $R_T\to A_T$. The pullback tensor theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] supplies these functors. Define the comparison $e_S^*Rq_{*,R}L\to Rq_{*,A}e_P^*L$ to be the adjunct of
$$q_A^{-1}e_S^*Rq_{*,R}L\cong e_P^*q_R^{-1}Rq_{*,R}L\xrightarrow{e_P^*(\varepsilon_{q,R,L})}e_P^*L.$$
The canonical derived adjunctions and the projection-mate normalization are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Restriction of scalars is exact because kernels and cokernels are the same underlying sheaves. Its total derived functor is therefore termwise restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], and it reflects isomorphisms by the cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. The two factorizations $(P,A)\to(P,R)\to(S,R)$ and $(P,A)\to(S,A)\to(S,R)$ have the same structural ring map; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies their derived direct images. Under this identification, the restriction of the displayed comparison is the $R$-projection map with $K=A_S$: both are adjunct to the same evaluation tensored with $A_P$. Here the ordered version is obtained by the two canonical tensor symmetries specified in the projection theorem; their naturality conjugates the usual counit-first mate into precisely this coefficient-first map. This can also be read as the tensor/exchange equality [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] for the commuting coefficient-change square of ringed topoi; that lemma explicitly does not require a Cartesian square of underlying topoi. Thus it is legitimate to test this $A$-linear comparison over $R$. On the source, scalar extension gives $A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S$; naturality of the projection mate identifies its components with the shifted twisted unit and the scalar-extended Kummer class that defines $h$ in the item. Derived tensor preserves isomorphisms, hence the resulting map is exactly $b_q$ and is invertible.

Define $t_q=\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1}$. Since $h=b_q\operatorname{in}_2$, $t_qh=1$ by cancellation. Under any change of Noetherian base $S'\to S$, the projective line and the line bundle with its displayed transition functions pull back to those over $S'$. Pullback of the equation $z^N=1$ identifies the twists, and the Kummer connecting homomorphism pulls back the class of the pulled-back line bundle, using [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. The unit components correspond because exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] is the mate of the inverse-image composition comparison: substituting its unit/counit formula on the unit of $q$ cancels the adjacent counit/unit by their triangle identity. The tensor comparison commutes with exchange by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. Consequently the square with $b_q$, $b_{q'}$ and the canonical proper exchange commutes. Inverting this square and composing with the second projection proves that $t_{q'}$ is the pullback of $t_q$. For arbitrary $K$ define $\epsilon_K$ by the displayed inverse projection formula followed by $1\otimes t_q$ and the tensor unit [lem-kun-tensor-unit]. Naturality gives a natural transformation $FG\to1$, where $F=Rq_*$, $G=q^{-1}(-)\otimes_A^LA_P(1)[2]$. The same tensor/exchange equality shows that these actual maps $\epsilon_K$, not merely their isomorphism classes, commute with base change.

Let $W=P\times_SP$ and $\Delta:P\to W$ be the diagonal. On the finite-finite chart its equation is $u-t$; on the infinity-infinity chart it is again a difference of coordinates; on a mixed chart it is $1-tu$. A monic difference is a non-zero-divisor over any base ring, and multiplication by $1-tu$ is injective by comparing the lowest total degree in a nonzero polynomial. Thus $\Delta$ is an effective Cartier divisor, and remains one after every base change here. Apply [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] to obtain $\delta:R\Delta_*A_P\to A_W(1)[2]$. Since $p_a\Delta=1_P$, derived pushforward composition [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives $R(p_a)_*R\Delta_*A_P=A_P$. We claim $t_{p_a}R(p_a)_*\delta=1$ for both $a$. This is an endomorphism of the degree-zero sheaf $A_P$, so its equality with identity is an equality of sheaf morphisms. Subtract identity and take the image sheaf. By exactness of stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], if the difference is zero on every stalk its image has zero stalks. [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to $0\to\operatorname{im}(f-1)$ then makes the image zero, hence $f=1$. Proper exchange [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring], supported Kummer base change and step 4 identify its geometric stalk with the integral of the supported class of one rational point of $\mathbf P^1_k$. Forgetting support gives that point's Kummer Chern class by the supported lemma. By [def-sc-pic0] its degree is one. The degree/Kummer identification in step 2 therefore sends it to $1\in R$; scalar extension in step 3 sends it to $1\in A$, and projection onto the degree-two summand is exactly $t_{p_a}$. This proves both identities, including over disconnected or nonreduced bases. Only morphisms of degree-zero sheaves, not arbitrary derived morphisms, were tested for equality on stalks.

source.place: Proof of diagonal integrals, with the ordinary finite-ring supported class

proof.text:
For $M\in D(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, projection for the proper closed immersion $\Delta$ identifies $R\Delta_*A_P\otimes_A^Lp_1^{-1}M$ with $R\Delta_*M$, because $\Delta^{-1}p_1^{-1}M=M$. Define
$$\eta_M:M\cong R(p_2)_*R\Delta_*M\longrightarrow R(p_2)_*(p_1^{-1}M\otimes_A^LA_W(1)[2])\cong q^{-1}Rq_*M\otimes_A^LA_P(1)[2].$$
The middle arrow uses $\delta\otimes1_M$ followed by the canonical tensor symmetry $A_W(1)[2]\otimes p_1^{-1}M\to p_1^{-1}M\otimes A_W(1)[2]$, using the preceding projection identification. This is the symmetry-conjugated ordered projection convention of step 1; the degree-two shift contributes sign $(-1)^{2i}=1$ on degree $i$ of $M$. For the last isomorphism, write $A_W(1)=p_2^{-1}A_P(1)$, apply the inverse projection formula for $p_2$, and then invert the canonical proper exchange $q^{-1}Rq_*M\to R(p_2)_*p_1^{-1}M$. These are isomorphisms on all complexes by [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring], not just on $D^+$. Pullback tensor comparisons are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the identity $R(p_2)_*R\Delta_*=1$ is the composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Every arrow is natural in $M$, so this defines $\eta:1\to GF$.

Check the first triangle $\epsilon_{FM}F\eta_M$. Use $qp_1=qp_2$, the direct-image composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], and the tensor/exchange equality [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. They identify this composite with
$$Rq_*M=R(qp_1)_*R\Delta_*M\xrightarrow{R(qp_1)_*(\delta\otimes1)}R(qp_1)_*(p_1^{-1}M\otimes A_W(1)[2])\cong Rq_*(M\otimes R(p_1)_*A_W(1)[2])\xrightarrow{Rq_*(1_M\otimes t_{p_1})}Rq_*M.$$
Here the trace on $p_1$ is the base change of $t_q$ by step 4. For the compatibility of these particular arrows, take the projection map to be the adjunct of the pullback tensor comparison followed by counit tensor identity, and exchange to be the adjunct of the square comparison followed by the pulled-back counit, as in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. In the two possible orders (exchange then projection, projection then exchange), their transposes are equal by the cited tensor/exchange coherence. For a composite pushforward the evaluation is $\varepsilon_{p_1}\circ p_1^{-1}\varepsilon_q$ after pullback composition: substituting this into the projection mate gives the iterated projection, since naturality moves $\varepsilon_q$ past the intervening tensor comparison. This also explains the interchange of $qp_2$ and $qp_1$: both evaluate the same two coordinate pullbacks through their composite, with the square comparison inserted once. Naturality of the $p_1$ projection with respect to $\delta$ makes the middle map, after the first projection identification, $1_M\otimes R(p_1)_*\delta$. Thus the entire composite is $Rq_*(1_M\otimes(t_{p_1}R(p_1)_*\delta))$, which is $1_{FM}$ by step 5. This is an equality of derived morphisms proved by mates, not by stalkwise detection.

source.place: Proof, first triangle and canonical-mate interchange

proof.text:
For the second triangle substitute $M=GK$ in step 6. The equality $p_1^{-1}q^{-1}K=p_2^{-1}q^{-1}K$ lets the $p_2$ projection formula take the common coefficient $q^{-1}K$ out of the pushforward. The canonical pullback tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] also identifies $p_1^{-1}A_P(1)$ and $p_2^{-1}A_P(1)$ with the one twist from $S$. Under these identifications, $\eta_{GK}$ is identity on $q^{-1}K\otimes A_P(1)[2]$ tensored with the arrow $R(p_2)_*\delta:A_P\to R(p_2)_*A_W(1)[2]$. The arrow $G\epsilon_K$ is identity on the same coefficient tensored with $t_{p_2}$: step 4 identifies this trace with $q^{-1}t_q$, and the tensor/exchange coherence [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] identifies its inverse projection with the one used in step 6. Cancelling these canonical inverse projection and exchange maps yields
$$G\epsilon_K\,\eta_{GK}=1_{q^{-1}K\otimes A_P(1)[2]}\otimes(t_{p_2}R(p_2)_*\delta)=1_{GK}.$$
The last equality is step 5. The interchange of the two copies of the unshifted twist is also identity: by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] it is locally free of rank one, and on a trivializing etale cover $ae\otimes be\mapsto be\otimes ae=ab(e\otimes e)$ by commutativity of $A$. Equality of these sheaf maps can be checked on that cover. Only shifts by $2$ are interchanged with tensor factors, so the Koszul factor is $(-1)^{2i}=1$ in every degree $i$ of $K$. With both triangles proved, the Hom bijections are explicitly $a:FM\to K\mapsto G(a)\eta_M$ and $b:M\to GK\mapsto\epsilon_KF(b)$. Naturality and the two triangles show that their composites are identities. This constructs $F\dashv G$ with precisely the stated counit, for arbitrary unbounded $M,K$.

Finally the unit in step 6 commutes with a base change $S'\to S$: the diagonal equation pulls back to the diagonal equation; its supported Kummer class pulls back by [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]; the tensor/projection comparison commutes with exchange by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. The remaining proper exchanges paste canonically. To see this on maps, expand each exchange as the mate in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. In two successive squares substitute the composite evaluation $\varepsilon_v\circ v^{-1}\varepsilon_u$; naturality commutes the intermediate inverse-image comparison past $\varepsilon_u$, and the adjacent unit/evaluation cancels by the original pullback/direct-image triangle. The remaining transpose is exactly the outer square comparison followed by its pulled-back counit. The adjunction bijection therefore identifies the pasted exchange with the outer exchange, including for unbounded arguments. Thus the unit and the counit of step 4 pull back to the very unit and counit constructed over $S'$. Along with step 4 this proves compatibility of the decomposition, trace and normalized adjunction. When $N=1$, $A=0$ and all derived categories are zero, so all constructions give the unique adjunction and the assertions still hold; the empty base is equally harmless.
